sources.entry: oneDNN - Generates VNNI and AMX kernels at run time under PyTorch, TensorFlow and OpenVINO, and calls Compute Library on Arm.

summary.one_liner: oneDNN is an open-source, cross-platform C/C++ library of optimized deep learning primitives (matmul, convolution, attention, normalization) for CPUs and Intel GPUs, and the acceleration layer behind PyTorch, TensorFlow, and OpenVINO.
summary.what_it_does: The library provides optimized implementations of matrix multiplication, convolution, attention, normalization and other deep learning operations. On Intel 64/AMD64, AArch64, and RISC-V CPUs it detects the ISA at runtime and JIT-generates kernels specialized for that instruction set. It supports f32, bf16, f16, f8, f4, u8/s8 and u4/s4 data types with various quantization schemes, including OCP microscaling formats. Post-ops fuse activations, residual connections and quantization into matmul and convolution, and the Graph API fuses larger patterns such as scaled dot-product attention and grouped-query attention. CPU threading can use OpenMP, TBB, or custom threadpools; GPU execution uses SYCL or OpenCL, with experimental NVIDIA and AMD GPU backends. The README's Quick Start builds a matmul performance example against a conda-forge install.
use_cases: accelerate deep learning inference on Intel or AMD CPUs
fuse attention and convolution post-ops for faster models
backend for PyTorch, TensorFlow, or OpenVINO kernels
run deep learning ops on Arm AArch64 servers
notable: Runtime ISA detection with JIT-generated kernels specialized to the CPU
Graph API fuses patterns such as SDPA and GQA
Supports OCP microscaling and many low-precision data types
Optional Arm Compute Library integration on AArch64
Used as the acceleration layer in PyTorch, TensorFlow, OpenVINO, ONNX Runtime and llama.cpp
caveats: Power ISA (PPC64) and IBMz (s390x) support is experimental with limited validation
NVIDIA and AMD GPU support is experimental
Arm Compute Library must be downloaded and built separately (minimum version 53.1.0)
Linux and Windows reset GPUs when kernel runtime exceeds several seconds unless hangcheck or TdrDelay is adjusted
README says deep learning practitioners should use frameworks rather than oneDNN directly
keywords: speed up neural network on cpu
